newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco stocks off amid new testimony vs industry.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco stocks off amid new testimony vs industry.

text.p: Tobacco stocks softened Friday amid new testimony from an industry insider that tobacco giant Philip Morris ordered the destruction of crucial research documents on the health effects of smoking.

Shares in Philip Morris were down 1-3/4 at 127-7/8 in afternoon trade on the New York Stock Exchange after falling as much as 3 points earlier in the day. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp was down 1/8 to 37-1/2.

Ray Morgan, who worked as an analytical chemist at Philip Morris for 20 years, said he was ordered in the 1980's to shred research reports that showed high concentrations of a carcinogen in cigarette smoke.
Morgan also testified that Philip Morris research tests used cigarettes that contained fewer chemical additives than cigarettes actually sold to consumers.

"There's a bit of uncertainty about how this will effect ongoing negotiations the companies are supposedly having to settle its suits. It could run up the cost of the settlement or put off the talks," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood.
"This is just another piece of the story. There is a belief that they have not been as forthcoming as they could have been," Brown said.
On top of Morgan's testimony, the tobacco industry this week has been sued by three more state attorneys general seeking to recover state Medicaid funds used to treat tobacco-related injuries.
Hawaii, Wisconsin and Indiana filed suits, bringing the total of state Medicaid suits to 22. Several counties, cities and other municipal governments have filed additional, similar suits.
One trader also said a Wall Street Journal article about research into tobacco marketing to minors also spooked investors on Friday.
Tobacco stocks had rallied earlier in the week amid reports the industry had taken steps toward settlement litigation.
Industry sources said major tobacco comapnies have hired two law firms and a public relations firm to consider possible parameters for a broad settlement.
